insights.headline: Gold climbs back to $4,148 as Fed hike bets reset; silver firms to $59.62
insights.summary: Gold recovered toward $4,150 on October 9 as softer US jobless claims and divided September Fed minutes reshaped rate expectations, with traders pricing an 18% chance of an October hike and 81% for December. On MCX, gold held near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams while silver stayed under pressure around ₹2.2 lakh per kg. Record third-quarter ETF inflows and China's 23-tonne September buying underscored resilient demand despite the price correction.
points: Spot gold +0.3% to $4,147.77 and December futures +0.4% to $4,172.70 on Oct 9 after a two-month low; CME FedWatch: 18% October hike odds, 81% December.
MCX December gold held near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on Oct 8; silver fell 1.24% to ₹2.20 lakh per kg as the dollar and yields capped gains.
Gold ETFs drew a record $31 billion in Q3, pushing holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes even as gold fell 8.5% in September.
China added about 23 tonnes of gold in September, its largest monthly buy in three years and the 23rd straight month of purchases.
RBI intervention held the rupee near 96.78 per dollar; banks have paid 3% IGST on bullion imports since the 2017 relief ended.

trending.title: Fed minutes reprice hike bets; gold rebounds
trending.summary: Most Fed officials expect another hike by year-end, but trimmed October odds (18%) after softer jobless claims were enough to lift spot gold back toward $4,150.

trending.title: ETFs and central banks absorb the correction
trending.summary: Record $31B of Q3 ETF inflows took holdings to 4,256 tonnes while China bought 23 tonnes in September — institutional demand stayed firm through the price slide.

trending.title: Domestic market: steady gold, weaker silver
trending.summary: MCX gold held near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams while silver lagged near ₹2.2 lakh per kg; analysts see crude, yields and the dollar capping upside with $4,090–$4,200 the range to watch.

trending.title: Rupee and tax frictions at the margin
trending.summary: RBI action kept the rupee just off its record low, while the end of bank bullion IGST relief adds a 3% tax layer to imports — both feed through to Indian retail gold prices.

items.title: Gold nudges higher with inflation risks, Fed rate path in focus
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,147.77 in early Asian trade on October 9, recovering from a two-month low, while December futures gained 0.4% to $4,172.70. Reuters reports inflation risks and the Fed's rate path are driving the rebound: St. Louis Fed's Musalem said another hike is needed to reach 2% inflation, while traders price 18% odds for October and 81% for December. Silver added 0.5% to $59.62.

items.title: Comex gold settles 0.44% higher at $4,131.80 as traders digest Fed minutes
items.summary: Gold futures recovered from a two-month low on October 8 as traders digested September FOMC minutes showing most policymakers expect another rate hike by year-end. December gold rose 0.5% to $4,161.10 while the front-month contract settled 0.44% higher at $4,131.80; silver fell 1.1% to $59.62. Markets priced an 18% chance of an October hike and about 80% for December, per the CME FedWatch tool.

items.title: Gold steady near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on MCX; silver under pressur: Key levels to watch
items.summary: MCX December gold held near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on Thursday, up 0.07%, while December silver fell 1.24% to ₹2.20 lakh per kg. Analysts cited a firm dollar, Fed rate-hike expectations and elevated crude; Anand Rathi's Vedika Narvekar sees a near-term downward bias with support near ₹1.44 lakh, while IBJA's Prithviraj Kothari flagged $4,000 an ounce as the next key level for gold.

items.title: Gold ETFs drew a record $31 billion in Q3; holdings hit an all-time high
items.summary: World Gold Council data shows global physically-backed gold ETFs attracted $10 billion in September, capping a record $31 billion third quarter. Holdings rose 67 tonnes to a record 4,256 tonnes even as gold fell 8.5% in September; assets under management slipped 7% month-on-month to $574 billion on the lower price. The US led inflows; UK funds had their strongest quarter on record.

items.title: Silver's long-term outlook remains bullish as new investment products offer income opportunities
items.summary: Amplify ETFs' Nate Miller says silver's long-term uptrend is intact: spot near $59 an ounce is down on the day but well above last year's roughly $50, supported by solar and industrial demand. New covered-call ETF products let investors earn income from the non-yielding metal, broadening its buyer base.

items.title: China ramps up gold buying as prices fall
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added about 740,000 ounces (roughly 23 tonnes) of gold in September, its largest monthly increase in three years and the 23rd straight month of buying, taking advantage of September's roughly 6% price decline. World Gold Council data shows central banks bought about 5.5 million ounces in the first eight months of 2026, led by China and Poland.

items.title: Gold, silver futures: Vandana Bharti on what’s capping upside on precious metals, range to watch
items.summary: SMC Global Securities' Vandana Bharti said elevated crude prices, bond yields and a firmer dollar are capping gold's upside, with support near $4,090 and resistance at $4,200; she expects the broader uptrend to resume once the rise in bond yields pauses. She sees MCX gold in a ₹1,45,000–₹1,52,000 range and MCX silver between ₹2,20,000 and ₹2,30,000 per kg.

items.title: MCX gold trades lower around ₹1.49 lakh; crude jumps as Iranian attacks on tankers continue
items.summary: MCX December gold futures traded about 0.4% lower near ₹1,49,450 per 10 grams on October 7 as a stronger dollar weighed, while December silver fell 1.1% to ₹2,24,782 per kg. Brent crude held above $101 a barrel after Iranian strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping inflation and Fed-hike bets in focus.

items.title: RBI intervention halts rupee's slide to record low, risks linger
items.summary: The rupee closed nearly flat at 96.78 per dollar on Thursday, just off its all-time low of 96.96, as likely RBI intervention kept it from testing record lows. Brent crude jumped more than 4% to $104.30 on Middle East supply worries while the dollar hovered near 18-month highs. Traders say the RBI's first rate hike in nearly four years is unlikely to slow record capital outflows.

items.title: India ends IGST relief on bank bullion imports; 3% tax applies since April
items.summary: Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava said banks have paid 3% IGST on gold and precious-metal imports since April 1, 2026, after the 2017 exemption was not extended. The decision, placed before the GST Council this week, puts banks and nominated agencies on the same tax footing as bullion exchanges. The levy is paid upfront and claimed as input tax credit, raising working-capital costs.

items.title: Senco Gold Share Price Gains Over 9% After Q2 FY27 Performance Report
items.summary: Senco Gold's shares jumped over 9% after its Q2 FY27 update showed total revenue up 31% YoY and retail revenue up 29%, with same-store sales growth of 19%. The jeweller crossed Rs 5,000 crore in H1 revenue and Rs 10,000 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis; diamond jewellery revenue grew 31% in value. Six new showrooms took the network to 215 stores.

items.title: PC Jeweller share price jumps over 7% on Q2 update | Stock up 54% YTD — What lies ahead?
items.summary: PC Jeweller's shares jumped over 7% after its Q2 FY27 update reported revenue up 28% YoY and confirmed debt-free status, clearing dues with all 14 consortium banks. The stock is up 54% in 2026, reflecting the turnaround from its debt-resolution phase. The update adds PC Jeweller to a string of jewellers reporting strong September quarters ahead of the festive season.
